back2basics.text: The right to privacy is a fundamental right protecting individuals' personal information and dignity. Freedom of speech and expression allows citizens and the media to communicate and receive information freely. Balancing these rights is essential in a democracy, especially with digital data and media evolving rapidly.

body.label: DNPA's petition
body.text: The Digital News Publishers Association contends that the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and its 2025 Rules violate journalistic freedom by imposing restrictions that conflict with constitutional rights to information and free speech.

body.label: Constitutional concerns
body.text: The petition argues the law contradicts the Supreme Court's privacy judgment affirming privacy as fundamental to human dignity and life, and infringes on Article 14 and 19(1)(a) protections.

body.label: Impact on journalism
body.text: The law subjects publishers, editors, reporters, and correspondents to requirements like prior consent, compelled erasure, and notice, which the DNPA says threatens all journalistic activities including those by whistleblowers and RTI activists.

sections.heading: What is the nature of the challenge against the privacy law?

body.label: Section 36 and Rule 23
body.text: These provisions grant the Central government broad, unchecked powers to requisition information from data fiduciaries or intermediaries without judicial oversight, necessity, proportionality, or notice to affected individuals.

body.label: Threat to journalistic sources
body.text: The petition highlights that such powers risk identifying and targeting journalistic sources, undermining confidentiality essential to press freedom.

body.label: Amendments to RTI Act
body.text: Section 44(3) of the DPDP Act amends the Right to Information Act to place all categories of 'personal information' beyond disclosure, effectively barring access to information relating to public offices.

sections.heading: Which specific provisions are contested and why?

body.label: Freedom of press at stake
body.text: The challenge raises the issue of whether privacy laws can unduly restrict the fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression, which is vital for a functioning democracy.

body.label: Balancing privacy and transparency
body.text: The case tests how India balances the right to privacy with the public's right to information and the media's role in holding power accountable.

body.label: Implications for digital governance
body.text: The outcome will influence how digital personal data is regulated in relation to journalistic activity and the transparency of public offices under digital public infrastructure.

sections.heading: Why does this matter for Indian democracy and governance?

back2basics.text: Inter-state boundary disputes arise when two states claim jurisdiction over the same territory. Article 131 of the Constitution grants the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in disputes between states, but with limitations. The Supreme Court can only adjudicate these disputes if they involve questions of law and not if barred by specific provisos. Often, such disputes require political or parliamentary resolution rather than judicial intervention. Maintaining status quo means no administrative or electoral changes should occur in the disputed area until resolution.

2026-10-27-pm-478d5bc1fe.deck: The Odisha government filed a contempt petition in the Supreme Court challenging Andhra Pradesh's notification for elections in the disputed Kotia group of villages. This case highlights constitutional and federal issues related to state boundaries, elections, and judicial authority.

structure.intro: Capacity building is essential for strengthening healthcare systems to effectively manage substance use disorders.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Capacity Building Programme for Drug De-addiction Services launched in 2026:
1. The programme aims to train 10,000 healthcare service providers by 2028-29.
2. The training is coordinated by the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS, and includes online and offline components.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: A careless reader might confuse the coordinating institution or the training methods; both statements are correct as per the evidence.

body.label: Programme launch and aim
body.text: The programme was launched on October 26, 2026, to strengthen the capacity of healthcare professionals in prevention, identification, assessment, treatment, and management of substance use disorders across India.

body.label: Training targets
body.text: It aims to train 10,000 service providers including doctors, nurses, counsellors, and allied healthcare personnel by March 2029.

body.label: Training methods
body.text: The programme uses a blended learning approach with online live sessions, self-paced online modules, and offline in-person training.

body.label: Institutions involved
body.text: Six central government institutions under the Drug De-addiction Programme (DDAP), coordinated by the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS, implement the training.

sections.heading: What is the Capacity Building Programme for Drug De-addiction Services?

body.label: National goal of Nasha Mukt Bharat
body.text: The programme supports the Government of India's commitment to achieve a Nasha Mukt Bharat by 2029 through coordinated multi-ministerial efforts.

body.label: Whole-of-government approach
body.text: Effective substance abuse control requires synergy between healthcare, social welfare, and law enforcement agencies to address prevention, treatment, enforcement, and trafficking.

body.label: Addressing coordination gaps
body.text: The Vision Document on Narcotic Control: 2026-2029 identifies gaps caused by fragmented departmental efforts and calls for sustained inter-ministerial coordination and accountability.

body.label: Capacity building as a key strategy
body.text: Strengthening treatment services and healthcare professional capacity is central to improving evidence-based addiction care and expanding access.

sections.heading: Why does this programme matter for public health and governance?

body.label: Training curriculum
body.text: The curriculum covers various substances including alcohol, cannabis, opioids, sleeping tablets, and inhalants, and addresses specific groups such as women and adolescents.

body.label: Training delivery
body.text: Doctors receive weekly 12-week online live sessions combining theory and clinical case discussions; nurses, CHOs, and ANMs have self-paced online modules; offline training is also provided.

body.label: Participant nomination
body.text: Participants are nominated by State Governments through the National Health Mission and by Central Government services including Armed Forces and Central Armed Police Forces.

body.label: Certification and resources
body.text: Certificates are issued upon completion, and resources like the second edition of 'Substance Use Disorder: Manual for Physicians' guide clinical practice.

back2basics.concept: Supreme Court Collegium and Judicial Appointments
back2basics.text: The Supreme Court Collegium is a body of senior Supreme Court judges responsible for recommending appointments and transfers of judges in the higher judiciary. It ensures judicial independence by limiting executive interference in appointments. The Collegium system is a key feature of the separation of powers in India's constitutional framework.

2026-10-27-pm-cd989606f7.deck: The Supreme Court Collegium has proposed four judges for appointment as Chief Justices of the High Courts of Gujarat, Delhi, Telangana, and Uttarakhand. This update is relevant for understanding the judicial appointment process and the separation of powers in India.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court Collegium's recent recommendations:

2. Justice P. Sam Koshy, whose parent High Court is Telangana, has been proposed for Delhi High Court Chief Justiceship.
mcq.trap: The trap is in the parent High Court of Justice P. Sam Koshy; his parent High Court is Chhattisgarh, not Telangana.

body.label: Four Chief Justices recommended
body.text: The Collegium proposed Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak for Gujarat High Court, Justice P. Sam Koshy for Delhi High Court, Justice Tapabrata Chakraborty for Telangana High Court, and Justice Sudhir Singh for Uttarakhand High Court.

body.label: Current and parent courts
body.text: Justice Pathak is currently a judge at Gujarat High Court with Gauhati as his parent court; Justice Koshy serves at Telangana High Court with Chhattisgarh as his parent court; Justices Chakraborty and Singh belong to Calcutta and Patna High Courts, respectively.

body.label: Additional appointments
body.text: The Collegium also approved the appointment of Ajay Sharma and advocate Vaibhav Anant Sugdare as judges of the Bombay High Court.

body.text: The Supreme Court Collegium plays a key role in recommending judges for High Court Chief Justiceships, illustrating the judiciary's independence in appointments.

body.label: Separation of powers
body.text: These appointments highlight the balance of power between the judiciary and the executive, a critical aspect of constitutional governance.

back2basics.text: The CBD is a global treaty aimed at conserving biological diversity, promoting sustainable use of its components, and ensuring fair benefit-sharing from genetic resources. It convenes Conferences of Parties (COP) where member countries negotiate frameworks and commitments to protect biodiversity. National strategies translate these global frameworks into country-specific targets and actions.

2026-10-27-pm-fbbb6bfb3e.deck: At the 17th Conference of Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP-17) in Yerevan, Armenia, India reiterated its dedication to biodiversity conservation and effective implementation of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. This is important for UPSC aspirants as it highlights India's environmental diplomacy, national biodiversity strategies, and multilateral cooperation efforts.

structure.intro: India reaffirmed its commitment to biodiversity conservation at CBD COP-17, aligning global frameworks with national priorities.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about India's commitments at CBD COP-17:
1. India supports benefit-sharing from digital sequence information on genetic resources through the Cali Fund.
2. India has established 1,134 Ramsar sites as part of its biodiversity conservation efforts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because India has 103 Ramsar sites, not 1,134; 1,134 refers to Protected Areas.

body.label: Biodiversity conservation pledge
body.text: India reaffirmed its commitment to conserving biodiversity and strengthening collective efforts to live in harmony with nature.

body.label: Global Biodiversity Framework alignment
body.text: India emphasized that implementing the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework must align with national priorities, circumstances, and legislation.

body.label: Support for finance and technology transfer
body.text: India called for adequate and predictable finance, capacity-building, and technology transfer from developed countries to support biodiversity governance.

body.label: Benefit-sharing on genetic resources
body.text: India supports benefit-sharing from digital sequence information on genetic resources through a multilateral mechanism, including the Cali Fund.

body.label: Science-based approach
body.text: India advocated a science-based, risk-proportionate, and precautionary approach to synthetic biology and biosafety.

sections.heading: What commitments did India reaffirm at CBD COP-17?

body.label: National Biodiversity Strategy
body.text: India’s updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan translates the Global Biodiversity Framework into 23 National Biodiversity Targets and 142 indicators.

body.label: Protected areas and heritage sites
body.text: India has 1,134 Protected Areas, 103 Ramsar sites, 57 Biodiversity Heritage Sites, and 18 Biosphere Reserves, including 13 under UNESCO’s Man and the Biosphere Network.

body.label: Conservation initiatives
body.text: Initiatives include the International Big Cat Alliance, Mission LiFE, Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam, MISHTI for mangrove restoration, Amrit Dharohar for wetland conservation, and the Soil Health Card Scheme.

body.label: Legislative alignment and local participation
body.text: India has aligned its legislation with the Convention and established village-level committees for decentralized access and benefit sharing, enabling local participation.

sections.heading: How is India advancing biodiversity conservation nationally?

body.label: Multilateral cooperation
body.text: India reaffirmed its commitment to work with all Parties to advance the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework under the spirit of 'One Earth, One Family, One Future.'

body.label: Hosting appreciation
body.text: India appreciated the Government of Armenia for hosting the 17th meeting of the CBD, reflecting diplomatic engagement in global environmental governance.
